Direct shear test on PS soil at relative density 0.33 to 0.53; apparatus: direct shear (University of Notre Dame); loading: normal stress 2935 psf. Recorded: shear stress and dilation vs shear displacement. One of 6 tests of this soil and density at normal stresses from 35.1 to 210.7 kPa, the family the report used to draw the failure envelope.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The numbers below were digitized from the published figure by two readings made separately; they agree within the stated reading bounds at 92 of the 116 points, and 20 are still under review. Student reviewers have looked at 19 of the 116 points on the scan; two reviewers confirmed 4 of them (see the provenance page). The test setup is incomplete: specimen height, displacement rate are not reported.
:::

## Data

![shear stress and dilation (normal displacement; positive up) against shear displacement, SI units, this test in red and the other tests printed in Fig. C-2B in gray. Error bars are reading bounds (half-widths from the digitization), not standard deviations. Filled markers were agreed by both readings, hollow ones were not.](../img/plots/b68-ds-fc-2b-n2935.png){.lightbox}

Peak shear stress 160.5 kPa at 5.70 mm shear displacement; 159.7 kPa at 6.32 mm, the end of the record. Dilation -106 micrometers at the end.

Download: [observations.csv](../files/data/experiments/b68-ds-fc-2b-n2935/observations.csv) (116 points: 41 plotted symbols, 72 samples of the drawn curve; columns `x_si`, `y_si` with bounds `x_bound_si`, `y_bound_si`; panel 1: shear stress in Pa against shear displacement in m; panel 2: dilation (normal displacement; positive up) in m against shear displacement in m; the printed-unit values, the pixel position on the scan and the review status of each point are kept in further columns) and [series.json](../files/data/experiments/b68-ds-fc-2b-n2935/series.json) (units, conversion factors, how the points were read).

Reading bounds on this figure (how far our reading of the printed figure may be off, not the uncertainty of the test): typical bound 8 micrometers in shear displacement, 989 Pa in shear stress (0.6 percent of the peak), 57 micrometers in dilation. Both independent readings agree within these bounds at 92 of the 116 points; 20 are still under review (hollow in the plot) and 4 were settled against the scan. [Check the digitized points against the scan](../figures/index.qmd#check-fc-2b).
